original_package.source_title: Data from: Study Green turtles (Chelonia Mydas) Hays Chagos Archipelago Western Indian Ocean

estimand: X: direct unsmoothed horizontal GPS cell-use distribution overlap for each pair, first 30 days post original source deployment; each animal's daily position mass normalized first, each observed animal-day has equal weight; each dyad cell intersection ∑ min(p_i(cell),p_j(cell)); 66 dependent pairs of 12 animals
projection: Lambert cylindrical equal-area (standard parallel 0°) x=R*lambda, y=R*sin(phi), R=6371.0088km; source lon/lat in degrees; no location rows exported
inference_limits: Grid 25km source provisional was selected before the first X calculation, but it is too coarse relative to the ≈12km full cohort early-period range and returns nearly unit overlap. Finer 0.1-2km sensitivity was added after inspecting the unexpectedly near-unity coarse result, so these are explicitly exploratory, not preregistered tests.
Estimated 2D overlap of recorded GPS fixes does NOT equal actual simultaneous co-presence, trophic/dietary resource sharing, or competitive niche overlap.
66 pairs repeat the same 12 tracked animals; no CI or statistical significance is assigned. Per-animal-day balancing reduces sampling effort concentration but not animal dependence.
All release sites are reported Diego Garcia in original reference, but exact environmental and trophic resource availabilities were not validated.
Original dates are only used to align the first 30 post-deployment days; exact locations/animal IDs are not republished.
Coarse grid masking shows apparent geographic sharing is scale-sensitive in this particular source, not a universal law.
R, T, E and calibrated 3D-Z source axes are not estimated; their status is NOT ESTIMABLE or UNTESTED, not zero.
